chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Dawud ibn Isḥaq al-Ḥaddā' from Muhammad ibn al-'Isṣ who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbidding the use of narcissus (for scent). I said, 'May I be your ransom, for what reason is that?' He said, 'Because it is the scent of the foreigners (non-Arabs/Persians).'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), peace be upon him
key_terms.النَّرْجِسِ: Narcissus (a type of flower used for scent)
key_terms.الْأَعَاجِمِ: The foreigners (specifically Persians in this context)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imams forbid or dislike the use of narcissus scent?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against using narcissus (anjerish) specifically because it was culturally identified as the scent of the Persians (A'ajam), illustrating the principle of 'urf (custom) in determining ritual preferences. This hadith, found in al-Tusi’s al-Istibsar, highlights how early Shia jurisprudence integrated social customs and cultural associations into rulings on purity and worship, distinguishing between intrinsic impurity and culturally specific dislikes.
